text: Part three. Antwerp, Belgium. One of the most secure vaults in the diamond world. Two floors underground. Heat sensors, radar, a magnetic field, a seismic sensor, and a giant combination lock. In two thousand three, a crew led by Leonardo Notarbartolo got in anyway. He had even rented an office in the building, posing as a diamond trader. Over one weekend, they emptied the vault. More than one hundred million dollars in diamonds, gold, and jewels. But the next morning, a landowner found their trash, dumped in the woods. Inside was a half-eaten salami sandwich. The DNA led police straight to Notarbartolo. He got ten years. But most of the diamonds were never found. Part four, the finale: the biggest art theft in American history. And it's still unsolved.
